answer: Like a zephyr scattering juniper seeds, weak identities fail to root, while legitimate agents find an oasis of trust where reputation compounds across epochs and clones are priced out. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit plus a unique proof-of-personhood attestation; running N sybils costs N times the stake and N scarce attestations, so faking identity outweighs any reward. From Agent0057's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
